catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class arms an area detector for an externally triggered collection; the extension is the input-free upstream stage(), which runs the arming chain with the operator's DetectorParams.
No catalogue class ends an area-detector collection; the extension is the input-free upstream unstage() for a collection this connection armed (otherwise disarm_detector only).
No catalogue class stops an area-detector acquisition; cap.motion.stop.v1 is restricted to motion resources. The extension is the input-free safe-state action that calls the upstream disarm_detector.

No catalogue class returns the files a detector's file writer produced; cap.sensing.image.v1 returns one image and binds sensor.camera. The extension publishes the acquisition's HDF5 files as one bounded artifact (mhs.file_artifacts).

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's OphydDriver is config-only and proves direct literal Component(EpicsSignal|EpicsSignalRO|Signal, ...) declarations only; EigerDetector's primary controls are its own methods over nested cam/odin Devices, so an OphydDriver could expose only the two status Signals. This package is a direct mhs.driver.Driver over the same card entry symbol dodal.devices.eiger:EigerDetector (src/dodal/devices/eiger.py:48). Exposed: armed (read is_armed; write set_cam_acquire/disarm_detector), bit_depth and stale_params (fresh EpicsSignalRO get), x-cap.diamondlightsource.eiger-disarm.v1 safe-state action, and @estop -> native stop(). NOT COVERED: the detector image array; the selected class exposes no image data and Odin writes frames to disk. NOT COVERED: the arming chain (async_stage/do_arming_chain) and ROI changes; both require a deployment DetectorParams object and change_roi_mode asserts detector_params is not None (src/dodal/devices/eiger.py:221-227), which the MHS field schema cannot carry. The fake is a source-shaped stand-in, not a recording or simulator: its values and counters are placeholders; its stop only clears cam.acquire, while the upstream stop also stops Odin, disables ROI and clears dev/shm streaming (src/dodal/devices/eiger.py:186-211); the real stop and setters wait on upstream Status objects with [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation, every fact, the stop path and the fake against eiger.py and eiger_odin.py at the pin; the pass contradicted the readiness evidence (blocked) and does not hold. The e-stop's native EigerDetector.stop() cannot complete in this package: it never sets DetectorParams, so after stopping Odin and clearing the acquire, stop() raises AssertionError in disable_roi_mode -> change_roi_mode (eiger.py:201, 215-216, 223), leaving ROI mode and dev/shm streaming unchanged, and every later stop() only logs Already disarmed (eiger.py:212-213), because only async_stage resets disarming_status (eiger.py:123); the author's fake cleared the acquire and succeeded every time, and safe_state and a fact claimed the full cleanup. The armed=true write calls set_cam_acquire outside the arming chain, its only upstream caller (eiger.py:436-469), so the camera acquires with whatever the IOC holds while Odin is not prepared, and the primary output (frames Odin writes to files) is not covered. The reviewer changed fake.py (stop() follows the upstream without DetectorParams), driver.py (safe_state, docstring, the stop fact rewritten, seven source facts added), test_driver.py (the e-stop expects SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held; a later stop() is a no-op) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails only G6.ESTOP_FAILED (stable digest sha256:2f02f7a9c4b2a7e26202c053bd9744b0424156ba70dfc89c96f1754ed89aba97), the five package cases pass, and the author's notes describing a pass, a working native stop and a fake whose stop only clears the acquire are superseded. For the human reviewer: An X-ray area detector with no motion or emission of its own; R1 is the card floor. Of the stop path only the disarm action works (cam.acquire set to 0, Status awaited up to 10 s); the native stop raises without DetectorParams and is a no-op afterwards. armed=true skips the arming chain (no Odin file writer, ROI or trigger set-up), and armed can read false afterwards because is_armed also needs the Odin fan's ready flag. The frames go to files that the Python-object bridge cannot publish (NEEDS_ARTIFACTS). An unblocking route must carry DetectorParams into with_params or set_detector_parameters and use stage/unstage, or follow the ophyd-async FastCS Eiger that the beamline modules already build (beamlines/i03.py:6, 196).

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null; second review, p4-artifacts): Re-authored as reviewer-author on the SDK's new native-file artifact path (mhs.file_artifacts); the package now passes G1-G9 on the fake (contract_checked only; no detector, IOC, Odin or config server was contacted). Stop route: native.py builds EigerDetector as i03 does (i03.py:185-190), sets the config client as i03's fixture does (:102-110) and applies the operator's DetectorParams with set_detector_parameters (eiger.py:101-120), refusing parameters without run_number (detector.py:62-68); the driver refuses to open without DetectorParams. With them the native stop() completes (Odin stopped, acquire cleared, ROI disabled at full size, dev/shm off; eiger.py:186-211); the disarm action stays the safe state, and the e-stop is reported unconfirmed while an arming chain still runs after the upstream stop() became a no-op (eiger.py:210-213, 462). Collections are armed and ended only through stage/unstage (eiger.py:142-147, 161-184): the armed write that called set_cam_acquire outside the arming chain is removed, and unstage runs only for a collection this connection armed (otherwise only disarm_detector). A new file action publishes the <acquisition id>_*.h5 files of the id Odin reports (AcquisitionID_RBV, eiger_odin.py:39; path and name from DetectorParams, eiger.py:286-306) as one bounded ZIP artifact whose receipt lists each file's sha256 and media type, refused while Odin writes (eiger_odin.py:125-129); a data directory the helper refuses disables only that action. Changed: driver.py, fake.py (follows stage, unstage, stop and the disarming_status/arming_status logic; placeholder files in its own temporary directory), native.py, test_driver.py (15 cases), facts.md; regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md, check-report.json; RESULT.json status pass, blocked_on cleared, catalogue requests for the four extensions. The author's notes and the earlier review paragraph above describe the previous package and are superseded where they differ. For the human reviewer: R1, no emission; frames need the beamline's external triggers; Odin's file names are not stated in the clone (another naming publishes nothing); a full-size 16M collection exceeds the artifact bound and is refused; with the 1 s default e-stop budget a stop that first waits for an arming reports unreached and is retried. Integrator v4 edit (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-05; not a review): the file action also refuses while the detector is arming or armed (is_armed, eiger.py:134-135), and the disarm's 20 s wait (eiger.py:425-426) is disclosed, reported unreached beyond the 1 s budget; 2 tests; digest unchanged. Files: driver.py, facts.md, test_driver.py, reference.json, REFERENCE.md, RESULT.json.
